condition_specific: Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma, colon cancer, skin cancer, leukemia, testicular cancer, multiple myeloma, prostate cancer, breast cancer, pancreatic cancer
filing_deadline_notes: May use presumption for up to 5 years after most recent date of qualifying exposure
notes: Applies to full-time paid firefighters in fire departments recognized by state fire marshal's office and manned by full-time paid employees. Must have 5+ consecutive years of service. Must have been exposed to heat, smoke, fumes, or carcinogenic/poisonous/toxic/chemical substances while performing firefighter duties. Cancer screening exams required by condition type: NHL/colon/skin/multiple myeloma exam required after July 1 2019; leukemia/testicular exam required after July 1 2022; prostate/breast/pancreatic exam required after July 1 2025. Secondary employment or lifestyle habits may be considered. Rebuttable by competent medical evidence; oncologist (board certified) for death claims.

condition_specific: disease or cancer (broad — any disease or cancer)
notes: Applies only to counties with a metropolitan form of government with population 400,000+ (per 1980 or subsequent federal census) — effectively Nashville/Davidson County. Applies to full-time firefighters required to work in toxic environments. May be established by ordinance. Pre-employment physical must have failed to reveal evidence of cancer. Does not affect rights under § 7-51-201.

Applies to full-time employees of a regular fire department in a state, municipal corporation, or political subdivision that has established compensation beyond workers' compensation. Pre-employment physical must have failed to reveal evidence of the condition.

Applies to EMTs and paramedics employed by a county with population over 400,000 (per 1980 or subsequent federal census) or a municipal corporation within such county, within the fire department, where compensation beyond WC has been established. Pre-employment physical must have failed to reveal evidence of condition.

§ 7-51-201(a) establishes a presumption of occupational causation for hypertension and heart disease among law enforcement officers generally, originally enacted in 1965 (Acts 1965, ch. 299). It is not itself a workers' compensation statute; rather, it establishes a presumption of occupational causation that attaches to whatever compensation program a covered government employer has set up for line-of-duty injury or death. It has been applied as part of workers' compensation claims where a municipality has opted into workers' compensation coverage (see Stone v. City of McMinnville (1995) and Krick v. City of Lawrenceburg (1997)).

It also explicitly covers correctional security employees of the Departments of Correction and Children's Services, and full-time county deputy sheriffs in correctional security positions. It is not itself a workers' compensation statute; rather, it establishes a presumption of occupational causation that attaches to whatever compensation program a covered government employer has set up for line-of-duty injury or death. It has been applied as part of workers' compensation claims where a municipality has opted into workers' compensation coverage (see Stone v. City of McMinnville (1995) and Krick v. City of Lawrenceburg (1997)).

condition_specific: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus), hepatitis C virus
filing_deadline_notes: Incident/accident report must be filed within 7 days of the exposure event. Post-termination coverage for 1 year from last actual date of service.
notes: Applies to full-time firefighters, paramedics, EMTs employed by state or political subdivision. Requires prior negative test for infectious disease before diagnosis. Worker must file a sworn declaration that they have not engaged in any high-risk behavior (outside-employment exposure, unsafe sexual practices, IV drug use, blood transfusion). Post-termination coverage: 1 year from last service date. Does not apply to death benefits under Tennessee consolidated retirement system or state death benefit. Pre-employment HIV testing required from July 1 2012; all infectious diseases from July 1 2015.

condition_specific: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD); workers' compensation presumption
notes: True workers' compensation presumption under § 7-51-206, covering full-time paid firefighters in departments recognized by the TN State Fire Marshal, effective January 1, 2024 (Public Chapter 465). Qualifying traumatic incidents include: witnessing the death or injury of a minor who subsequently died; witnessing an individual's death involving serious bodily injury shocking the conscience; responding to an event where a victim sustained serious bodily injury shocking the conscience; or responding to an event where a co-worker, responder, or family member sustained serious bodily injury or died. PTSD must be diagnosed by a mental health professional within 1 year of the firefighter's final date of employment. The presumption is rebuttable by a preponderance of evidence that the PTSD was caused by non-service-connected risk factors. This is separate from, and in addition to, the § 8-50-119 treatment access mandate, which is tracked as its own entry in this dataset.

Tennessee Public Safety Behavioral Health Act requires public safety employers (including those employing firefighters and EMTs) to provide at least 10 PTSD treatment sessions via health benefits, maintain lists of qualified mental health providers, and prohibit retaliation. This is a treatment access mandate, NOT a WC presumption. Does not apply to workers' compensation plans under title 50. Effective July 1, 2018.
